subject: 9Router HTTP executor retry behaviour for openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free
finding: HTTP executor retries happen at the transport layer, below the task-level max_attempts_per_provider=1 guard. A 503 from OpenRouter causes 4 total upstream attempts (1 original + 3 retries) to the SAME route before the executor fails. 200 and 429 cause exactly 1 attempt each.
scope_of_retry: Same model, same provider, same exact URL — no paid model substitution or provider fallback observed in offline test. E4_PROVIDER_PREFERENCES (allow_fallbacks:false, only:nvidia) preserved on every attempt.
paid_substitution_risk: NOT OBSERVED in offline test. Routing controls (allow_fallbacks, only, max_price:0) are preserved on each retry attempt per offline evidence.

resolution_options.description: Explicitly document that 503 retries are same-model/same-provider with max_price:0 enforced. Allow up to 4 attempts as a verified bounded behavior, not a new capability.
resolution_options.risk: Low — no paid substitution observed; free-quota exhaustion possible across 4 attempts but cost remains $0

resolution_options.description: 9Router source reads STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS etc from process.env. However, the retry table (p constant) is hardcoded in the bundle — no documented environment variable override exists for retry counts.
resolution_options.note: No env-var retry override found in installed source

resolution_options.option: C — Owner explicitly accepts 503 retry behavior in final canary grant
resolution_options.description: Final inference approval grant explicitly states: maximum_upstream_attempts=4 (1+3 retries on 503), all on same model/provider, max_price enforced throughout.

recommended_resolution: Option C — include explicit 503-retry acknowledgment in the final inference grant. The task-level max_attempts_per_provider=1 in e4-worker.mjs prevents RE-DISPATCH to a different provider; the transport retries are same-model only. This is behaviorally bounded and safe for a zero-price free-model canary.
